question_en:
I am compiling a dual-unit index for the volcanoes in the attached regional map. Please start from the third red triangle from the top in the diagram; thereafter, compare only the vertical positions of the triangle tips, moving each time to the volcano whose triangle tip is immediately below the current marker (horizontal position does not affect the order). When the elevation on the official page first drops below **2,500 m**, include that volcano in the results and then stop. Please answer the following questions:
1. Which volcanoes were visited in order? What are their respective `Elevation` (in meters and feet) and `Volcano type`? At which volcano did the route finally stop?
2. How many different official volcano pages were verified in total during this process?

Answer Format: Please answer in numbered points (1)—(2). For question 1, use a table to list the volcanoes in order, their elevations in both units, and their types; include a "Continue/Stop" column to indicate the endpoint, without needing to separately name the stopping volcano. For question 2, provide the total number of pages in text.
answer:
(1)

| Visit Order | Volcano | Elevation (meters) | Elevation (feet) | Volcano type | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Mount Rainier | 4,392 m | 14,410 ft | Stratovolcano | Continue |
| 2 | Mount Adams | 3,742 m | 12,277 ft | Stratovolcano | Continue |
| 3 | Mount St. Helens | 2,539 m | 8,330 ft | Stratovolcano | Continue |
| 4 | Mount Hood | 3,426 m | 11,240 ft | Stratovolcano | Continue |
| 5 | Mount Jefferson | 3,199 m | 10,495 ft | Stratovolcano | Continue |
| 6 | Three Sisters | 3,157 m | 10,358 ft | Complex volcano | Continue |
| 7 | Newberry | 2,434 m | 7,986 ft | Shield-shaped Composite | Stop |

(2) A total of 7 different official volcano pages were verified.
